name: Pictorialism
summary: Photography that borrows the look of drawing and etching. Soft-focus lenses, hand-worked pigment prints and warm toning blur the line between a photograph and a painting, to claim the status of art.

philosophy.core_thesis: A photograph is art when the maker's hand shows in the image, so the print must look made and not recorded.
design_principles: Soften the image with a soft-focus lens or a diffusion filter so that edge sharpness falls to about 60% of a sharp lens.
Hold the tonal range narrow: lift the black point to 12–18% and roll the highlights off at 92–95%.
Tone the print warm: shadows near #3A2E26 and highlights near #E8DCC6, as in platinum or gum bichromate.
Light the subject from a large soft source, such as a north window or overcast sky, at a key-to-fill ratio of 2:1.
Compose like a picture: a few big tonal masses, a low horizon and a figure or object set slightly off centre.
Choose subjects with a mood, such as mist, evening, a pool, a woman in a loose dress or a bare tree, over a record of fact.
anti_patterns: Crisp edge-to-edge sharpness and visible lens detail
Hard specular highlights and pure white paper
Saturated colour or a cool neutral grey print
Modern subjects shown without atmosphere, such as signs, cars and screens
Digital sharpening halos and clean clinical noise reduction
A flat documentary viewpoint at eye level with no tonal design

composition.framing: A vertical or square-ish plate with generous empty space; the subject fills at most 40% of the frame.
composition.viewpoint: Eye level or slightly low, at 3 to 10m, with no wide-angle distortion.
composition.geometry: Big simple masses: a diagonal of mist, a curve of a bank, a single vertical tree; no sharp crossing lines.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre on a third line, with a quiet area of tone on the other side.

principles.rule: Leave 40–60% of the frame as quiet tone: mist, water or sky.
Set the figure on a third line, within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.
Keep the luminance step between figure and ground at 15–25% of the tonal range, so that edges melt.
Use 1 toning hue for the whole print and 0 second hues; vary only tone, in 3 to 5 steps.

light.quality: Soft and diffused, from window light, shade, mist or overcast sky, with no hard shadow edge.
light.direction: From the side and slightly above, or behind the subject for a rim of haze.
light.colour_temperature: 6500–7500K (overcast and shade); the warmth comes from the print, not the light

lens_and_camera.format: Large format glass plate or sheet film, 5×7 in or 8×10 in, printed by contact
lens_and_camera.aperture: f/4.5 to f/8 with a soft-focus lens; f/16 with a pinhole or a plain lens and a diffusion filter
lens_and_camera.focus: Focus on the subject and let the soft-focus lens spread the spherical aberration; the eye falls on one small sharp area.

colour_and_grade.treatment: Monochrome with a warm or cool single-hue tone. The tone belongs to the paper and the pigment, so colour does not vary inside the image.
grade_recipe: Convert to monochrome with a gentle red filter mix (R 60, G 40, B 0) to calm skin.
Lift the black point to 15% and cap the white point at 94%.
Lower midtone contrast by 20% with a long, flat S-curve.
Split-tone: shadows #3A2E26 at 30% strength, highlights #E8DCC6 at 20%.
Add a soft-focus layer: Gaussian blur of 1% of the long edge, 40% opacity, in Screen mode.
Add paper texture at 8% opacity and a vignette of −12%.
colour_and_grade.grain: No film grain; a fine paper-fibre texture instead

subject_and_staging.staging: The photographer arranges the figure, the costume and the setting, as a painter would, before the exposure.
subject_and_staging.direction: Quiet, introspective poses, with the head turned away or the gaze lowered.

workflow: Develop the negative, then retouch it with pencil or etching knife by hand.
Print by contact in platinum, or in gum bichromate over platinum in two or three layers.
Brush the pigment to remove detail in the areas that should stay soft.
Mount on a tinted board with a wide margin.
post_processing.output: A small, tactile print, 20 to 30 cm on the long side, in a wide mount.

canonical_works.work: The Soul of the Blasted Pine

emotion.target_response: Reverie and quiet: the viewer feels a remembered scene, not a recorded one.

avoid_when: The brief needs factual detail, product accuracy or legible small text.
The subject is a modern device or a fast action scene.

modifiers.how: Close the aperture to f/64, drop the diffusion and the hand work, and keep the large format and the tonal range wide; the print becomes crisp and cool.

grain.note: The plates were ISO 10 to 25; the domain floor is 25.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 305 to 406 mm on 8×10 in.

sources.title: Met Open Access 267838: Edward Steichen, The Flatiron, 1904 (cite only: the Met does not mark this object public domain)
